What happens when capitalism becomes so successful that the problem is no longer too little—but too much?
In Surplus , economist and market strategist Marc Chandler traces the extraordinary rise of economic abundance from the earliest agricultural civilizations to today’s world of overflowing capital, soaring asset prices and unprecedented productive capacity. He argues that many of the forces destabilizing modern societies—from widening inequality and financial speculation to political discontent and environmental excess—are symptoms of a profound transition: we have created an economic system extraordinarily good at producing wealth, but have yet to build institutions capable of managing its abundance.
Drawing on economics, history, politics and philosophy, Chandler shows how earlier surpluses transformed civilizations—and argues that today’s surplus gives us an opportunity to do so again. Marc Chandler - Tech Weakness, Rate Cut Realities, Presidential Cycle Playbook, Precious Metals Breakdown

The KE Report
2d ago • 19 mins
In this Daily Editorial, Cory and Shad welcome Marc Chandler, Chief Market Strategist at Bannockburn Capital Markets and editor of Marc to Market, for the weekly market recap and look ahead to next week. With crucial central bank decisions and top-tier GDP data on deck, the discussion unpacks underlying crosscurrents across sovereign debt, energy, foreign exchange, and metals.
* Big Tech Fragility and Market Rotation: A breakdown of the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index’s continued pullback and whether the market’s defensive posture signals true institutional risk-off positioning or routine month-end rebalancing.
* Yield Curve Conundrum vs. Surging Oil: Why benchmark Treasury yields are retreating even as WTI crude presses multi-week contract highs, and what this divergence suggests ahead of the FOMC meeting.
* The "Rate Cut" Reality Check: An examination of Fed funds futures pricing, persistent US consumer strength, and why aggressive easing bets may remain premature.
* Historical Election Cycle Tailwinds: What historical data reveals about third-year presidential cycles and how that seasonal tendency could shape equity performance into next year.
